title: Build Velocity Audit
summary: Analysis of development speed and deployment efficiency.
content:

2026-03-10 -- Elon

2. AOM-STUDIO REPO (Website)

First commit: 2026-02-05 00:40 AZ Latest commit: 2026-03-10 19:04 AZ Total commits: 181 Active days: 12 Calendar span: 34 days (but with a ~3 week gap)

Phase 1: Manual Builds (pre-Claude Code)

Date What happened
Feb 5 Repo created. Package.json, basic React/Vite/Tailwind scaffold. 13 commits.
Feb 9 Biggest manual build day. 19 commits. App.jsx updates all day.
Feb 10 Continued manual iteration. 13 commits.
Feb 11 Image uploads, more App.jsx work. 19 commits.
Feb 12 2 commits. Slowing down.
Feb 13 2 commits. Nearly stopped.
Feb 17 4 commits. Quick touch.
Feb 22 1 commit. Last manual activity.

Phase 1 totals: 73 commits over ~17 days. Sporadic after Feb 11. This was Patrik building solo, by hand, in the GitHub web editor.

Phase 2: Agent-Driven Builds (post-Claude Code, Mar 7+)

Date Commits What shipped
Mar 7 10 Dashboard (Mission Control), kanban, agent roster, council modal
Mar 8 50 Mobile responsive, command bar, agent tools, brand page, site architecture overhaul, waitlist form, preloader optimization
Mar 9 34 Brand guidelines (v1-v4), chat relay widget, Dark Frame redesign, QA fixes, overlay fix
Mar 10 14 Outreach plan page, growth plan page, /system page, HVAC research page, briefs hub (3 pages), /system sales page

Phase 2 totals: 108 commits in 4 days (Mar 7-10). That's 27 commits/day average, with Mar 8 peaking at 50.

The Gap

Feb 22 to Mar 7 = 13 days of zero activity. This is the gap between "doing it manually" and "doing it with agents." The moment Claude Code came online (Mar 5 in AOM-EA), the site repo lit up 2 days later with Bobby driving.

Key Pages: Build Times

Observation: By Mar 10, Bobby was shipping entire pages in single commits. The pipeline had fully matured. Early pages (dashboard, brand) required many iterations. Late pages (outreach, growth, system, briefs, HVAC) shipped as one-shots.

3. KEY BUILD TIMELINES

Zero to Multi-Agent System

  • Start: Mar 5, 10:16 PM (repo init)
  • 12 agents + skills + pipeline: Mar 10, 4:00 PM
  • Total: ~114 hours (~4.75 days)
  • This includes: 12 agents, 20+ skills, Telegram relay, email pipeline, calendar integration, QA system, production pipeline, auto-orchestration, phone home bridge

HVAC Research Page (Full Pipeline)

  • Council brief (strategy): Mar 10, 2:26 PM
  • Bobby builds page: Mar 10, 4:20 PM
  • Pipeline complete commit: Mar 10, 4:27 PM
  • Total: ~2 hours from council brief to shipped page
  • This is the full Alex > Bobby pipeline in action. By this point the agents knew their roles.

Jacob Outreach System

  • First commit (agent created): Mar 6, 11:55 PM
  • First email batch (19 Tier 1 drafts): Mar 7, 8:38 AM (~9 hours later)
  • Auto-send approved: Mar 9, 7:58 PM (~68 hours later)
  • Batch 4 (32 personalized emails): Mar 10, 10:33 AM
  • Total from zero to autonomous sending: ~68 hours (~2.8 days)
  • But the delay was intentional: DMARC propagation + Patrik approval gate. The system was ready to send within 9 hours.

/system Page (Steve's Content to Bobby's Build)

  • Steve agent created: Mar 10, 4:00 PM
  • Bobby builds /system V1: Mar 10, 3:55 PM (actually started before Steve was formally created, from council output)
  • Bobby builds /system V2 (sales page): Mar 10, 7:04 PM
  • Total: ~3 hours from concept to polished sales page

Dashboard (Mission Control)

  • First commit: Mar 7, 4:33 PM
  • Full-featured (kanban, agents, command bar, mobile, council, chat relay): Mar 9, 2:09 AM
  • Total: ~34 hours for full ops dashboard
  • But V1 was live within 1 hour of first commit.

AOM Website Redesign (Dark Frame + Bold Graphic)

  • Brand guidelines research + Steffen specs: Mar 8, 6:50 PM
  • Bobby applies to full site: Mar 9, 6:51 AM
  • Elmo QA pass: Mar 9, 12:05 AM (next day)
  • Total: ~12 hours from brand direction to QA-passed site redesign

4. VELOCITY COMPARISON: MANUAL vs AGENT

Metric Phase 1 (Manual, Feb 5-22) Phase 2 (Agent, Mar 7-10)
Calendar days 17 4
Total commits 73 108
Commits/active day 10.4 27
Pages shipped 1 (homepage, unfinished) 10+ (dashboard, brand, social, outreach, growth, system, HVAC, briefs x3, construction)
Features shipped Basic React app Full ops platform with 12 agents
Output quality "Update App.jsx" repeatedly Named features, QA-gated, pipeline-driven

Agent-driven development is 2.6x faster by commits/day and infinitely faster by feature output. Phase 1 produced a single incomplete page in 17 days. Phase 2 produced 10+ pages and a full ops dashboard in 4 days.

5. ESTIMATE VALIDATION: IS "7 DAYS FOR STARTER KIT" REALISTIC?

What "starter kit" includes (from latest-result.md):

  • Template context files (me.md, work.md, team.md, priorities.md, goals.md)
  • CLAUDE.md configured for client
  • Email outreach + calendar automations
  • Telegram relay (optional)
  • Setup scripts + quickstart guide

What the data says:

Deliverable Actual build time (AOM) Estimate for client Verdict
Context file architecture Hours 0-13 (~13 hours) 1 day Conservative. Could be 4-6 hours with templates.
CLAUDE.md entry point Hour 0 2 hours Accurate.
Email outreach pipeline Hours 25-34 (~9 hours for first batch) 2-3 days Conservative. Gmail OAuth is the bottleneck, not the code. With a playbook, 1 day.
Calendar integration Hour 23 (~1 hour of actual work) 30 min per client Accurate.
Telegram relay Hours 36-80 (~44 hours, but v1 was 36 hours) 1-2 days per client Slightly conservative. V1 took 1 day. V5-V7 iterations were AOM-specific hardening.
Decision logging Hour 0 (just a markdown file) 0 effort Accurate.
Starter kit repo template Not yet built 2-3 days Accurate. This is new work (templatizing, not building from scratch).

Verdict on 7 Days

Conservative, but honest. Here's the breakdown:

  • 48 hours (aggressive): Context files + CLAUDE.md + calendar + decision log + basic email outreach. No Telegram, no dashboard, no custom skills. This is the "turn the lights on" package.

  • 5 days (realistic): Everything in 48 hours + Telegram relay + polished email pipeline + 2-3 custom skills + onboarding guide. Client is operational.

  • 7 days (the estimate): Everything above + buffer for client-specific customization, OAuth troubleshooting, and documentation. This is the safe number to quote.

  • 10-14 days (premium): Add dashboard, QA agent, Mom-style orchestration, and training. This is Tier 3 territory.

The 7-day number is smart to quote because:

  1. AOM's system took 5 days but we were building the architecture for the first time
  2. Second build always goes faster (templates exist, patterns are known)
  3. Client environments have unknowns (their Gmail, their infra, their workflows)
  4. Under-promise, over-deliver beats the reverse every time

What Can Ship in Each Timeframe

48 hours:

  • Working executive assistant with context files
  • Calendar management
  • Decision logging
  • Basic email drafts (not auto-send)
  • "Talk to your assistant" guide

1 week:

  • Everything above
  • Email outreach pipeline (auto-send capable)
  • Telegram relay (mobile command center)
  • 2-3 custom skills for their workflow
  • Onboarding call + support

2 weeks:

  • Everything above
  • Custom dashboard
  • QA agent for their deliverables
  • Content/social media pipeline
  • Multi-agent orchestration
  • Full training session

6. RAW NUMBERS

Metric AOM-EA aom-studio Combined
First commit Mar 5, 10:16 PM Feb 5, 12:40 AM Feb 5
Total commits 280 181 461
Active days 6 12 --
Calendar span 5 days 34 days 34 days
Commits/active day 46.7 15.1 --
Peak day Mar 8 (103 commits) Mar 8 (50 commits) Mar 8 (153 combined)
Peak hour Mar 8 7-8 PM (41 commits) -- --

Mar 8 was the single most productive day: 153 commits across both repos. That's the day agents fully came online and started building autonomously.

BOTTOM LINE

The system went from nothing to a 12-agent AI operations platform with email, calendar, Telegram, QA, orchestration, and a 10+ page website in 5 days. That's not an estimate. That's what the git log says.

Quoting 7 days for a client starter kit is conservative and appropriate. The first build is always the hardest. Every subsequent client benefits from templates, playbooks, and lessons learned. If anything, the honest number for a basic setup is closer to 3-4 days, with 7 giving comfortable margin for client-specific friction.

The real proof point: on Mar 10 (today), Bobby shipped 6 new pages (outreach, growth, system x2, HVAC, briefs) in a single session. The pipeline is fast now. And it only gets faster.
